cohort: The study included 110,818 school children aged 6-18 years from six cities in the Pearl River Delta region of China.
finding: Exposure to higher tertiles of PM2.5 and its components, particularly organic matter and black carbon, was significantly associated with greater odds of childhood ADHD.
cross-section timing: Exposures were estimated using three-year average concentrations, and outcomes were measured via a survey of children aged 6-18 years.
